title: REC-04/C3: depth-verify basement room portal omissions before enabling hard occlusion
body:
Source: GPU acceptance C2 run [40410389913](https://github.com/mrcalzon02/The-Beckenburg-Project/actions/runs/40410389913) on commit `1918b289ec056618385c95ac1175b92a9bf8db3d`, uploaded artifact `beckenburg-van-house-viewport-profile/portal-candidate-audit.csv`. Test is functional/diagnostic-only and **passed**; however, audit warns against hard portal culling.

**Actual C2 CSV (per-camera, closed and opened first door):**
- Exterior rooms 14 and 13: zero missing frustum candidates.
- Ground-floor room 0, target 4: 8,847 authored frustum-intersecting faces, 425 *outside graph* (basement rooms `[10,11]`).
- Ground-floor room 4, target 8: 4,333 frustum-intersecting, 306 outside graph (`[10,11]`).
- Upper-floor room 8, target 4: 8,411 frustum-intersecting, 134 outside graph (`[11]`).
- Same counts whether the sampled first door is open or closed.

Important interpretation: **frustum-intersecting is not identical to depth-visible**. Rooms 10 and 11 are authored basement rooms at y=-3; floors/walls may occlude many of these faces. Do not declare an actual missing visible-pixel regression from the frustum-only evidence. Do not add number-specific room whitelists or turn on hard portal culling based on graph reachability.

**Next scoped implementation:** build a reproducible depth/occluder-aware visibility reference or compare rasterized pixel ownership with/without cautious portal rejection across these viewpoints, representative stair/floor void views, basement door states, and physical camera path. Count actual surfaced pixels/visibility targets, including transparent glass/windows. If any truly visible geometry is missing, fix general portal/vertical opening topology with authored spatial evidence. Keep simulation, ghosts, evidence and network authority wholly independent of visibility. Preserve screenshots/CSV, exact-SHA build and hardware checks. Tracks parent #7 and draft #17.
